note: 'By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. By faith he was commended as righteous ... And by faith he still speaks, even though he is dead' (Heb 11:4). **Genesis says the offering was accepted and does not say why** (Gen 4:4-5); Hebrews supplies the reason.
'By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, without knowing where he was going.' (Heb 11:8), and again at 11:17 offering up Isaac.
Named in the closing list at Heb 11:32.
Named in the closing list at Heb 11:32.
'By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death ... For before he was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God' (Heb 11:5), reading Genesis 5:24.
Named in the closing list at Heb 11:32.
'By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the future.' (Heb 11:20) -- a blessing Genesis 27 obtains by deception, recorded here without it.
'By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons and worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff.' (Heb 11:21).
Named in the closing list at Heb 11:32.
'By faith Joseph, when his end was near, spoke about the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones.' (Heb 11:22), which Genesis 50:25 records and Joshua 24:32 completes.

'By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter' (Heb 11:24), and kept the passover at 11:28. **A refusal counted as an act of faith**, which is the only one in the chapter.
'By faith Noah, when warned about things not yet seen, in godly fear built an ark to save his family.' (Heb 11:7). **Moved with fear** -- the chapter does not treat fear and faith as opposites here.
'By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies in peace, did not perish with those who were disobedient.' (Heb 11:31). **The epithet is kept**, in a chapter of commendation.
Named in the closing list at Heb 11:32.

'By faith Sarah, even though she was barren and beyond the proper age, was enabled to conceive a child ... because she considered Him faithful who had promised' (Heb 11:11). **Genesis 18:12 has her laugh at the promise**, and Hebrews names her among the faithful without mentioning it.
'By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to follow, they were drowned.' (Heb 11:29).
'By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch Israel's own firstborn.' (Heb 11:28).
